annotator_note: D5. Q asks for the caller procedure that makes Cobra deal with a single-dash long option token `-delete` the way git does. The Cobra-side code that does look at single-dash tokens does not bind them to long flag names: stripFlags (command.go:642-679) treats a single-dash token as a flag only when `len(s) == 2` (command.go:664), i.e. `-d`, and it only removes args for subcommand lookup rather than defining flag syntax; argsMinusFirstX (command.go:684 onward) repeats the same test. I therefore find related code but no contiguous span in a tracked, regular .go file at the pin that contains the mechanism or ordered steps Q expressly asks for; writing one would require synthesis from the pflag dependency and from git's own CLI behaviour, neither of which is in the pinned tree. This is not an effort-based finding: the pinned tree is 66 tracked files, I read every flag-parsing path in command.go and grepped the whole tree for single-dash, POSIX and Go-flag-package handling.

judgements.reason: The condition that makes it possible: Cobra adds its combined BoolP(help, h, ...) flag only when no flag named help already exists, so an application that declares its own --help (without a shorthand) and a separate -h flag keeps the two spellings as distinct flags.

The mechanism that decides the outcome: execute() short-circuits to the help path purely on the boolean value of the flag named help, which is why the default single flag makes -h and --help indistinguishable and why splitting them into two flags separates the behaviour.
Shows in Cobra's own code that a shorthand letter can already belong to a different flag than the long name being registered, so the long form and the single-letter form need not be the same flag.
The hook for customising what the help path does once it is reached.
